params.instruction: Build a compilable standalone TikZ figure (use \documentclass[tikz,border=5pt]{standalone}). Use pixel coordinates with y flipped: TikZ point = (x*0.01, -y*0.01) with a global scale, i.e. use \begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.01cm,y=-0.01cm] and the raw pixel coordinates. Points: A(54,34), B(431,175), C(54,175), D(168,77), E(290,411), N(101,52), unlabeled point P(204,175) on BC (do not label it). Draw solid segments: A-B (passing through N and D, which lie on AB), B-C, A-C, C-E, E-B, E-D, D-C. Draw the dashed segment N-C (perpendicular from C to AB, meeting AB at N), and add a small right-angle square mark at N on the side toward C/A (square of side ~12 px). Labels: A at upper-left of A, B at right of B, C at lower-left of C, D above-right of D (near (168,77), label offset to the upper-left/above since AB goes up-right), N just above-left of N, E below E. Use font \small or \normalsize, no grid, no axes. Labels should be placed with 'above', 'below', 'left', 'right' anchors outside the points, using node distance ~6 pixels scaled appropriately (remember y is flipped, so 'above' in the flipped system still means visually above). Keep line width ~0.8pt. Make sure it compiles.
